title: Functions, Docstrings & Tool Registration
why: LLMs cannot execute code on their own; they call functions you provide. The function name, type annotations, and docstring are converted into JSON schema and passed to the LLM.
objectives: Write structured docstrings that LLMs can parse
Build a tool registry pattern with decorators
concept: The docstring is literally the prompt that tells the LLM when and how to call your function. A poor docstring causes the LLM to hallucinate wrong parameters.

code.content:
from typing import Callable, Dict, Any
import inspect

TOOL_REGISTRY: Dict[str, Callable] = {}

def agent_tool(func: Callable) -> Callable:
    """Decorator to register python functions as agent tools."""
    TOOL_REGISTRY[func.__name__] = func
    return func

@agent_tool
def calculate_roi(investment: float, return_amount: float) -> float:
    """
    Calculate Return on Investment (ROI) percentage.
    
    Args:
        investment: Initial capital invested in USD.
        return_amount: Total final revenue received in USD.
        
    Returns:
        Calculated ROI percentage as a float.
    """
    if investment <= 0:
        raise ValueError('Investment must be greater than zer✅')
    return ((return_amount - investment) / investment) * 100

print('Registered Tools:', list(TOOL_REGISTRY.keys()))
result = TOOL_REGISTRY['calculate_roi'](1000.0, 1500.0)
print(f'ROI Result: {result:.1f}%')

practice.description: Write a tool get_stock_quote(symbol: str) with full Google-style docstrings and register it using the @agent_tool decorator.
practice.hint: Check inspect.getdoc(calculate_roi) to verify docstring extraction.

requirements: Inspect function signatures using Python inspect module
Automatically map function parameters to an LLM-compatible tool definition schema

Used decorators to build modular tool registries
Added defensive parameter validation inside tool bodies
mistakes: Missing parameter descriptions in docstrings leading to parameter confusion by the LLM
